title: fix(android): simplify setup and recover blocked permissions
body:
Related: #157409

## What Problem This Solves

Android setup shows a long permission list, and a permanently denied permission can leave users tapping a row without a way to recover.

## User Impact

Setup shows four optional choices: Notifications, Microphone, Camera, and Location. Other existing permissions stay available under **Additional features**. Users can continue without granting access. Denied requests offer the existing Android Settings recovery dialog, and rows refresh when users return.

Existing camera/location opt-in, applying choices on Continue, and Gateway reapproval remain unchanged. This deliberately covers setup and denial recovery only—not automatic first-use prompts or background permission notifications.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing setup models and Android launcher; connect its denial callback to the existing `PermissionRequester` recovery method. The earlier notification/agent-attribution system and all `SecurePrefs`, runtime, dispatcher, SMS, and protocol changes are removed from the PR.

The final diff is **6 files, +199/−27 lines**: two production files (+46/−14), two test files, one README line, and the generated source-string inventory. No new storage, migration, dependencies, or permission policy.

## Evidence

- Verified head: `b6c7081f51fb246e140532e8dddad5e327ce0ce1`.
- **164 tests passed, none failed or skipped**: `InitialOnboardingLayoutTest`, `OnboardingFlowLogicTest`, and `PermissionRequesterTest`, in Play and third-party variants. Both debug APKs build. Combined Gradle test/build wall time: **41.43 s**.
- Both new UI regressions fail on pre-PR source for the intended reasons: no Android Settings recovery after denial, and the old setup layout. The corrected tests deliver platform permission results through Android's existing dispatch path; Notifications, Camera, and Location recover, without implicitly enabling camera/location.
- Revision-scoped `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <six changed paths>` (including Kotlin lint and native schema guard), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent review: **P0–P2 scoped clean**, after the final reduction.
- CI: [CI run 36081981557](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36081981557) **passed** on the verified head, including Android Play/third-party/Wear tests, Kotlin lint, both native-access lanes, and `openclaw/ci-gate`. The exact-head security/dependency gates also passed.
- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157701#issuecomment-5824929985) completed on the verified head with no actionable findings.
- Production Compose screenshots below: SDK 34, dark theme, 360×720, isolated fixture restored at the permission step. Android result callbacks and Settings intents are exercised under Robolectric; no physical-device/emulator execution is claimed.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: existing long setup list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66f3c81f-2957-483f-8539-987cb8ba213b) | ![After: four optional choices and collapsed additional features](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a70c269-8337-434f-a3dc-de2c80eefeae) |

<details><summary>Measured test cost</summary>

The new denial/recovery case takes **2.479 / 1.188 s**, and the setup/skip case **2.720 / 3.146 s** (Play/third-party JUnit times). The entire existing layout test file takes **11.778 / 9.976 s**. CI test-step wall times (whole variant lanes, not individual new tests): **435 s Play**, **432 s third-party**, and **424 s Wear**.

Fixture corrections during development: settle Android's platform pending-request state instead of bypassing it with direct registry delivery; allow the queued dialog-button callback to complete before checking its Settings intent. No sleeps, retries, or weaker assertions were added.

</details>

Worked on by: @IWhatsskill
